en.headline: Health Department raids seven premises over unregistered cancer vaccine claims
en.dek: The Department of Health said a vaccine advertised as preventing multiple cancers is not a registered medicine in Hong Kong, and referred the case to Customs and the Medical Council.
body: The Department of Health said on Monday night that it was taking enforcement action after reports that a medical centre was offering customers a vaccine claimed to prevent many types of cancer. The department said the product is not a registered pharmaceutical product in Hong Kong, and that it had found no registration record with drug regulators on the mainland or overseas.

Officials said a complaint was received in July about social-media claims by a medical centre and related bodies. Inspectors have since carried out repeated surprise visits. On 31 August they inspected the centre and six other premises in Hong Kong and Kowloon, seven sites in all, and warned those in charge that illegally supplying an unregistered medicine is an offence under the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance.

The department said any advertisement claiming the vaccine can prevent cancer is misleading and may amount to fraud. It has already issued a warning letter over suspected breaches of the Undesirable Medical Advertisements Ordinance and required the advertisements to be taken down. The case has been referred to Hong Kong Customs over possible illegal import of unregistered products, and to the Medical Council because it may raise questions of professional conduct.

A department spokesman said health workers who tell patients that an unapproved product can prevent or treat cancer risk delaying proper care, which the department described as serious professional misconduct. The public was urged not to inject unknown substances on the strength of advertisements. From 2021 to June this year, the department said, 138 cases of selling or possessing unregistered products ended in conviction, with sentences of up to 10 months in prison or fines of up to 242,000 Hong Kong dollars.

zh.headline: 衞生署突擊巡查七處所 跟進未註冊防癌疫苗聲稱
zh.dek: 衞生署表示，有疫苗被宣傳可預防多種癌症，但並非本港註冊藥劑製品，個案已轉介海關及醫務委員會。
body: 衞生署周一晚表示，有報道指一間醫療中心向顧客提供聲稱可預防多種癌症的疫苗，署方正嚴肅跟進並展開執法。署方強調該款疫苗並非香港註冊藥劑製品，目前亦未發現內地或海外藥品監管機構有相關註冊紀錄。
衞生署指，七月接獲舉報，指一間醫療中心及關聯機構在社交平台聲稱可提供該疫苗。署方其後多次突擊巡查，八月三十一日再巡查該中心及港九另外六個處所，合共七個地點，並提醒負責人非法提供未經註冊藥物可干犯《藥劑業及毒藥條例》。
署方表示，任何廣告聲稱該疫苗可防癌均屬誤導，並涉嫌詐騙。署方早前已就懷疑違反《不良廣告（醫藥）條例》向有關公司發警告信，要求刪除相關廣告。個案已通報香港海關，跟進可能涉及未經註冊藥劑製品非法進口；因可能涉及醫生專業操守，亦已轉介香港醫務委員會。
發言人指，醫護人員若誤導病人，指未獲批核的疫苗具防癌或抗癌作用，可能令病人延醫，屬嚴重專業失德。市民切勿輕信廣告注射不明物質。署方指，二〇二一年至今年六月，共有一百三十八宗售賣或管有未經註冊製品個案被定罪，最高判監十個月或罰款二十四萬二千元。
